paper.title: On the Optimality of Batch Policy Optimization Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Batch policy optimization with finite-armed stochastic bandits (fixed counts n_i)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline (batch) policy learning from a fixed logged dataset with fixed per-arm counts n_i; no interaction with the environment.
unmapped: offline/batch setting: the learner receives n_i i.i.d. samples of each arm (counts fixed, not chosen) and outputs a single arm
settings.definition_quote: assume the action space consists of $k > 0$ arms, where the available data takes the form of $n_i>0$ real-valued observations $X_{i,1},\dots,X_{i,n_i}$ for each arm ... The (simple) regret of $\cA$ is defined as $\cR(\cA, \theta) = \mu^* - \EE_{X\sim \theta}[ \mu_{\cA(X)} ]$ ... we assume that the distributions $P_i$ are 1-subgaussian with means in the unit interval $[0,1]$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline (batch) policy learning from a fixed dataset; no interaction.
unmapped: offline/batch setting with fixed counts (n_1, n_2); algorithms use the sufficient statistic X_i ~ N(mu_i, 1/n_i)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the 2-armed bandit case ($k=2$) with Gaussian reward distributions $\cN(\mu_1, 1)$ and $\cN(\mu_2, 1)$ ... We assume that algorithms only make decisions based on the sufficient statistic ... $X=(X_1, X_2, \bn)$ with $X_i\sim \cN(\mu_i, 1/n_i)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Batch k-armed Gaussian bandit with weighted-minimax criterion (optimal value estimation difficulty)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline (batch) policy learning from a fixed dataset; no interaction.
unmapped: offline/batch setting with fixed counts n_i
regret weighted by E*(theta), the minimax-constrained difficulty of estimating mu* given a*
settings.definition_quote: Suppose that the reward distribution for each arm $i\in[k]$ is a Gaussian with unit variance. Consider the problem of estimating the optimal value $\mu^*$ where the optimal arm $a^*$ is also provided to the estimator.

algorithms.name: Confidence-adjusted index algorithm I(alpha) (argmax mu_hat_i + alpha/sqrt(n_i))
General index algorithm argmax mu_hat_i + b_i
Thresholding algorithm A_beta (choose arm 1 iff X_1 - X_2 >= beta/sqrt(n_min))

symbols.M_n: max over m in [k] of sqrt(max(1, log m)/n_m), with counts sorted n_1 <= ... <= n_k
symbols.n_m: number of samples of arm m in the dataset

conditions: counts n fixed and ordered n_1 <= ... <= n_k (wlog)

source.label: thm:minmax-lb
source.quote: Fix $\bn = (n_i)_{i\in [k]}$ with $n_1 \leq \cdots \leq n_k$. Then, there exists a universal constant $c > 0$ such that \inf_{\cA} \sup_{\theta\in \Theta_{\bn}} \cR(\cA, \theta) \geq c \max_{m \in [k]} \sqrt{\frac{\max(1, \log(m))}{n_m}}.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound on simple regret in batch setting; proved with Gaussian unit-variance instances.

symbols.n_min: minimum number of observations of any arm in the dataset

tuning: delta solves delta = sqrt(32 log(k/delta)/min_i n_i)
alpha in [-beta_delta, beta_delta], beta_delta = sqrt(2 log(k/delta))

source.label: thm:minimax-upper
source.quote: Fix $\bn = (n_i)_{i\in [k]}$. Let $\delta$ be the solution of $\delta = \sqrt{32 \log(k/\delta)/\min_i n_i}$, and $\cI$ be the confidence-adjusted index algorithm with parameter $\alpha$. Then, for any $\alpha\in [-\beta_\delta,\beta_\delta]$, we have \sup_{\theta\in \Theta_{\bn}} \cR(\cI(\alpha),\theta) \le 12 \sqrt{\frac{\log(k/\delta)}{\min_i n_i}}.

results.notes: Covers greedy, LCB and UCB. Remark 1: also holds with arm-dependent alpha_i in [-beta_delta, beta_delta]. Here delta is a data-independent analysis/tuning quantity determined by n_min and k.

symbols.g_i_star: min over eta of g_i(eta) = sum_{j>=i} exp(-n_j/2 (eta - mu_j - b_j)_+^2) + min_{j<i} exp(-n_j/2 (mu_j + b_j - eta)_+^2)

source.label: thm:instance-upper-general
source.quote: Consider a general form of index algorithm, $\cA(X)=\argmax_i \hat{\mu}_i + b_i$ ... Assuming $\mu_1\ge \mu_2\ge \cdots \ge\mu_k$, ... $\Prb{\cA(X)\ge i} \le \min\{ 1, g_i^* \}$ and $\cR(\cA) \le \sum_{2\le i \le k} \Delta_i \left(\min\{ 1, g_i^* \} - \min\{ 1, g_{i+1}^* \} \right)$ where we define $g_{k+1}^*=0$.

results.notes: sum over i=2..k with arms sorted; written using sum_subopt loosely (includes any arms tied with optimum, whose Delta_i=0).

symbols.Delta_h: gap of arm h = max{i: max_{j<i} L_j < max_{j'>=i} U_{j'}}, U_i = mu_i + b_i + beta_delta/sqrt(n_i), L_i = mu_i + b_i - beta_delta/sqrt(n_i)
symbols.Tail_h: sum_{i>h} (Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}) sum_{j>=i} exp(-n_j/2 (max_{j'<i} L_{j'} - U_j)^2)

source.label: coro:instance-upper-general-simplified
source.quote: Following the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:instance-upper-general}, consider any index algorithm and any $\delta\in(0, 1)$. Define $U_i=\mu_i + b_i + \beta_{\delta}/\sqrt{n_i}$ and $L_i = \mu_i + b_i - \beta_{\delta}/\sqrt{n_i}$. Let $h = \max\{i\in[k]: \max_{j<i} L_j < \max_{j'\ge i} U_{j'}\}$. Then we have $\cR(\cA) \le \Delta_h + \frac{\delta}{k}\Delta_{\max} + ...$

results.notes: Remark 2 relaxes this to Delta_h + delta*Delta_max.

symbols.B_greedy: min over i in [k] of (Delta_i + sqrt(2 log(k/delta)/n_i) + max_{j>i} sqrt(2 log(k/delta)/n_j)), arms sorted by decreasing mean

source.label: coro:ub-greedy-instance
source.quote: for any $0<\delta<1$, the regret of greedy ($\alpha=0$) on any problem instance is upper bounded by $\cR(\cA) \le \min_{i\in \iset{k}} \left(\Delta_{i} + \sqrt{\frac{2}{n_{i}}\log\frac{k}{\delta}} + \max_{j>i} \sqrt{\frac{2}{n_{j}}\log\frac{k}{\delta}} \right) + \delta$.

symbols.B_LCB: min over i in [k] of (Delta_i + sqrt(8 log(k/delta)/n_i))

source.label: coro:ub-lcb-instance
source.quote: for any $0<\delta<1$, the regret of LCB ($\alpha=-\beta_\delta$) on any problem instance is upper bounded by $\cR(\cA)\leq \min_{i\in \iset{k}} \Delta_i + \sqrt{\frac{8}{n_{i}}\log\frac{k}{\delta}} + \delta$.

results.notes: The min applies to the sum Delta_i + sqrt(...) per the proof.

symbols.B_UCB: min over i in [k] of (Delta_i + max_{j>i} sqrt(8 log(k/delta)/n_j)), arms sorted by decreasing mean

tuning: alpha = beta_delta = sqrt(2 log(k/delta)), any 0 < delta < 1

source.label: coro:ub-ucb-instance
source.quote: for any $0<\delta<1$, the regret of UCB ($\alpha=\beta_\delta$) on any problem instance is upper bounded by $\cR(\cA)  \le \min_{i \in \iset{k}} \left( \Delta_i + \max_{j > i} \sqrt{\frac{8}{n_{j}}\log\frac{k}{\delta}} \right) + \delta$.

symbols.beta_c: c*c_0 - 2, where c_0 is the minimax lower bound constant and c the minimax-optimality slack factor

conditions: k = 2 Gaussian arms with unit variance
ratio sup_theta R(A,theta)/R*_{M_{n,c}}(theta) where R* is the best regret on theta among c-minimax-optimal algorithms

source.label: thm:instance-negative-1
source.quote: Let $c_0$ be the constant in minimax lower bound such that $\inf_{\cA} \sup_{\theta\in \Theta_{\bn}}\cR(\cA, \theta) \ge c_0/\sqrt{n_{\min}}$. Then for any $c > 2/c_0$ and any algorithm $\cA$, we have \sup_{\theta\in \Theta_{\bn}} \frac{\cR(\cA, \theta)}{\cR^*_{\cM_{\bn, c}}(\theta)} \ge \frac{ n_{\min} }{ n_{\min} + 4 } e^{\frac{\beta^2}{4} +  \frac{\beta}{4}\sqrt{n_{\min}}  } where $\beta=cc_0 - 2$.

results.notes: Lower bound on the instance-optimality ratio (not regret itself); shows no instance-optimal algorithm. Corollary 5: for fixed pi_1, limsup_{n->inf} of the ratio is +infinity.

conditions: k = 2 Gaussian arms with unit variance
results.notes: Appendix proposition used in proof of Theorem 4. Proposition 4 gives the instance-dependent version.

symbols.n_total: |n| = total number of observations in the dataset

conditions: quantity is the weighted regret sup_theta R(LCB,theta)/E*(theta), E*(theta) = best error among minimax-optimal estimators of mu* given a*

source.label: prop:weighted-minimax-lcb
source.quote: For any $\bn = (n_i)_{i\in [k]}$, {\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_\bn} \frac{\cR(\lcbalg,\theta)}{\cE^*(\theta)}}<c\sqrt{\log |\bn|}, where $c$ is some universal constant.

results.notes: Proof notes the constant c may contain a log k term.

bound.regime: along a sequence of count vectors n_j

conditions: specific algorithm: UCB index algorithm (alpha = beta_delta)

source.label: prop:weighted-minimax-ucb-greedy
source.quote: There exists a sequence $\{\bn_j\}$ such that \limsup_{j\rightarrow\infty} \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\bn_j}}{\frac{\cR(\textnormal{UCB},\theta)}{\sqrt{\log |\bn_j|}\cdot \cE^*(\theta)}} = + \infty

results.notes: Shows UCB is not weighted-minimax optimal.

bound.regime: along a sequence of count vectors n_j

results.notes: Shows greedy is not weighted-minimax optimal.
